correctness.rationale: For integer q>=3 and fixed lambda, d(X,Y)>pi-epsilon is exactly d(X,-Y)<epsilon. The two latitude cap constraints become a>=-lambda and a+c<=lambda in t=epsilon a, s=epsilon(a+c), while tangent displacement h=(b,c) satisfies |h|<1 to leading order. The product spherical Jacobian is epsilon^(q+1)(1+o(1)) uniformly on bounded coordinates. Compact localization, boundary-null dominated convergence, and the normalizing cap area A0=sigma_q/2 give sigma_(q-1)J_q(lambda)/A0^2 and the uniform conditional tangent-bundle density on R_lambda. For lambda<=-1/2 the strict event is empty. Independently integrated J_3(lambda) at six values, including both support thresholds, and verified agreement with the displayed piecewise profile. These finite checks do not prove joint weak convergence; the local-coordinate argument does.
residual_risks: No uniformity as q->infty or for lambda(epsilon) outside compact sets; ambient distance only; conditional convergence excludes lambda<=-1/2.

value.rationale: The moving hemisphere is a natural geometric transition: the near-antipodal event disappears for lambda<=-1/2, then admits a constrained tangent displacement and eventually the full unit displacement ball. The complete normalized conditional law supplies more information than a tail scalar and resolves all parameters q>=3, lambda>-1/2 at the critical scale. The support change is mathematically motivated by the geometry of opposite caps.
residual_risks: Specialized to uniform round caps, fixed dimension and one joint critical scaling; does not claim a general stochastic-geometry universality theorem.

limitations: Finite independent checks corroborate only the stated cases; all-dimensional or asymptotic conclusions rest on the cited mathematical proofs.
